rv.q: Even in a concert staging, the momentum starts high and gets higher.
It's flesh and blood shaped by discipline and artistry into a parade of vital, pulsing talent.
Chicago - the best musical in London since the National'
Under Leigh Silverman's direction, the cast craftily exploits every comic opportunity, and smoothly inhabits David Korins'
Bebe Neuwirth is sensational as Velma, a sister convict Roxie shoves out of the spotlight.
It remains a heartening experience, a life-affirming dedication to the magic and art of theatre, and something that absolutely should not be missed.
If anything can revitalise the moribund West End and restore a jaded theatregoer's faith in the form, this is it.
What seemed cynical in 1975 is now au courant.

I am typically of the opinion that no show has any business occupying a Broadway house for more than a decade: Theater is ephemeral, and the magic tends to wear off as the years pass and performances become stale. ’Chicago’ makes this a difficult position to maintain. Ten thousand performances later, it's still dazzling.
For a Broadway musical that has lasted thousands of performances, 'Chicago' is in remarkably good shape.

cn.t: Critics praise this stripped-down revival as sharp, sassy, and wildly entertaining, with Kander and Ebb's score and Fosse-style choreography remaining potent after decades. The show defies expectations by staying vital and energetic.
